title: 20+ hours building a DECA prep site to help you this year
excerpt: Just another tool to help you and your students on their DECA success journey.
content:
I love building materials for DECA advisors and competitors, and my to-do list is really long. At the start of this season I wanted to create a DECA prep site that I wish I had to organize my students for DECA success. I hold back no secrets. My prep site, GOATs Get Glass, was built to simplify advising your chapter and deliver individualized prep plans for your students.

Monday I held a soft-launch with my first chapter using the site, and it didn’t break. Now I am excited to share the site with you!

**I will make a video showing all these features over the weekend. This is a longer post than normal. I’m really excited!!!

What’s inside

Here are important features I built for the site. You can see some of these for yourself in the my demo site (prep.thebowtiegoat.com/demo). Let me start with what I built for students, which will allow me to better explain what I built for you.

Features for Students:

  • A weekly prep plan. Once the advisor sets the competition dates, the site backmaps a plan from your start to competition day. Currently I have built an 8-week plan for role play events, a 16-week plan for prepared events, and a 8-week plan for professional selling events. Students see this week’s to-do list, and most tasks check themselves off when the work is done. Advisors can choose to use my plan, remove items, or add their own. I show your students exactly how I have led a chapter in the past.

  • Cluster exam tracker. This has always been my secret to DECA success. I finally built an exam tracker everyone can benefit from. Your students take a DECA exam they already have (District exams are free on DECA’s site), enter their answers on the site, and instantly see their score, every missed question with its PI and source, and where they rank from previous test takers. I have years worth of testing data. Now your students can compare how they do on exams to other competitors. A clear distinction here- I am NOT hosting DECA exams. That certainly breaks copyright laws. No DECA cluster exam questions exist on my site. If your students come to my site with the test, they can input their answers and get detailed feedback about their results.

  • Exam data. I really like exam data. I said that already, I think. Using the exam blueprint and how a student misses questions, my site generates a projected score for District, State, and ICDC. I have an Exam Deep Dive section under student results. It’s quite remarkable and difficult to explain here completely.

  • Role play tracker. You know what bothers me about role plays? Very few students track how they do on role plays! It is tough to get better on them without keeping track of your work! Now, students can practice and log their results after every practice run. Rather than focus on a score, I have the judge’s rubric level (Novice to Exemplary) on every row. I also provide a place for the judge’s feedback, and one thing to fix next time. If you choose to use my BowtieGOAT role plays (65 and counting), the site even tracks your ability to perform the role plays. If you bring your own DECA role play (again, I don’t link to any as to not violate copyrights), you can still log your results.

  • Performance indicator flashcards. Not a new feature, right? How is mine better? Every year a perform a thorough analysis of what PIs show up on which role plays. I have a Districts study deck matched to this year’s district instructional areas, plus an All PIs deck. I have only included PIs from the 600+ role plays I have saved locally. What does that mean? In a Business Admin Core event, nearly 2000 PIs exist in DECA’s PI document. I identified only 138 PIs that ever show up on role plays. These 138 should really help a student focus their prep! Sure other flashcard decks exist online. I am confident none of them are as focused on success as mine!

    Principles and Marketing are live now, with my goal of having all the clusters loaded by the end of the weekend. Every card a student misses gets tracked, just like exam misses, so they know what they keep missing. Eventually I plan to link the flashcard misses, exam misses, and role play PI data into the most challenging PIs a student needs to focus on. See where I am headed? If we track everything in one site, we can track so many patterns.

  • Written events. I wrote a 16-week plan that generically leads students through any written event. My site gives an organized place for teams to share their progress with you so you do not need to search email or shared drives. Also, teams share one plan and turn in links to their outline, drafts, and final paper inside the site so you can see their progress easily.

  • My results. Students will track a lot of different components on this site. The student’s “my results” page tracks their work in one convenient place.

Features for Advisors:

I really built this site for you. With 60 different DECA events, planning and managing the work above can be ANOTHER full time job. Here’s where you win!

  • A one-stop advisor dashboard. See every student’s progress in one quick page. You have to see it to believe it.

  • Adaptable prep plans. I know you have led successful chapters too. You can alter my prep plan to include additional items or remove unnecessary items. You have full control over the plan delivered to your students.

  • Simple stoplight tracking. With your chapter’s prep plan designed with weekly items, each of your student will have a simple stoplight to tell you what is going on. On track - slipping - or needs a nudge, based on their actual prep plan.

  • Who’s actually working. A “This week” column in your dashboard shows you the real work being done by students (exams, role plays, flashcards, tasks), not just recent logins. My favorite feature is a “Working ahead” tag tells you exactly who deserves a hallway high five!

  • See any student view. From the dashboard you can click a “view as a student” option to see what the student sees, if you need more detailed information. Importantly, your dashboard page is kept simple but links to details if you want them.

  • So much more. Pair teams, set competition dates, sign students up with a QR code, excuse tasks for a student who joined late, and add your own chapter items (”Mock competition Tuesday in Room 204”), archive students who sign up twice (it’s happened already), etc. Truly as we make it through this beta year, the features will adapt to your needs.

  • Site flags. Recommend a feature or send me a note directly from the advisor dashboard. I will review site flags, fix the urgent issues, and try to make substantive updates only on Saturday mornings (when all high school students are definitely NOT using a prep site)!

See it for yourself

I’ve built a lot and said a lot, but words can only go so far. So I built a demo. Go to prep.thebowtiegoat.com/demo and you’ll land in the Advisor Dashboard of GOAT Academy, a pretend chapter that’s always in week 4 of its prep plan. Click everything! It’s a sandbox, so nothing you do is saved, and refreshing the page starts it all over.

How do I sign up

As I shared two weeks ago, this year’s version is a pilot for annually paid subscribers of this Substack. Your whole chapter gets access. I’m keeping the group small on purpose. I’m sure some things will break (they already have, and I’ve already fixed them), but I’m also sure it will save you time this season. My local high school’s chapter is using the site- some of the students being students I teach. I will not let them down and I will not let you down. I will do my best to help your chapter get to ICDC this year.

Want your chapter on the site? If you already are an annual plan paid subscriber ($80), you will have received an email to sign up for the site. If you honor me by signing up as a paid subscriber here, I will set up your school within the week.

This year is a beta year. Next year will be version 1.0. If you are interested in helping me build the best DECA competition prep site online alongside me this year, let’s start this journey together.

One final thought

My goal hasn’t changed since I started BowtieGOAT. I want to do whatever I can to help advisors and students on their DECA success journey. We’re advisors who care deeply about our students, and we never have enough hours to do everything we want for them. I hope this site gives a few of those hours back to you.

P.S. If you’re wondering how one person built all this across 18 days as a dad of five with a full teaching schedule... I had help. The site was coded with Claude, (I will iron out the “Claude” feel in version 1.o) but every decision, every role play, and every prep plan came from ten years of getting students to the DECA stage. Built by BowtieGOAT. Coded with Claude.
